## Enhancement: Add explicit skill invocation rules to AGENTS.md

### Problem

AGENTS.md currently lists skills in the "Knowledge Resolution Order" as a general tier (`.cursor/skills/`), but it never tells the agent **which skill to read for which topic**. This means skill invocation depends entirely on Cursor's automatic skill-matching heuristic, which may not trigger consistently — especially for prompts that don't use the exact trigger phrases defined in the skill descriptions.

### Proposed Change

Add a new section to AGENTS.md (e.g., **"Skill Invocation Rules"**) that contains an explicit mapping from prompt topics to the skill that **must** be read and followed before any work begins.

Each entry should pair a set of topic keywords or task types with the corresponding skill path under `.cursor/skills/`, covering all 18 project-level skills:

| Topic / Trigger | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| Accessibility, WCAG, a11y, screen reader, keyboard nav | `accessibility`, `wcag-audit-patterns` |
| Authentication, sessions, sign-in, better-auth | `better-auth-best-practices` |
| Database, schema, migrations, Drizzle, queries | `drizzle-orm` |
| UI design, building pages/components, visual polish | `frontend-design` |
| Next.js conventions, RSC, metadata, error handling | `next-best-practices` |
| Caching, PPR, `use cache`, cacheLife, cacheTag | `next-cache-components` |
| App Router, streaming, parallel routes, data fetching | `nextjs-app-router-patterns` |
| E2E testing, browser automation, Playwright | `playwright-skill` |
| SEO, meta tags, structured data, sitemap, robots | `seo` |
| shadcn/ui components, Radix, forms with RHF + Zod | `shadcn-ui` |
| Tailwind v4 setup, theme, CSS variables, dark mode | `tailwind-v4-shadcn` |
| Advanced TypeScript types, generics, utility types | `typescript-advanced-types` |
| Component architecture, compound components, composition | `vercel-composition-patterns` |
| React/Next.js performance, bundle optimization | `vercel-react-best-practices` |
| Unit testing, mocking, coverage, Vitest | `vitest` |
| UI review, UX audit, design best practices | `web-design-guidelines` |
| Discovering or installing new skills | `find-skills` |

### What should be done

- Add the mapping table (or equivalent structured format) as a new section in `AGENTS.md`.
- For each entry, include a clear directive stating the agent **must read the skill file first** before proceeding with the task (e.g., *"When the prompt involves [topic], read `.cursor/skills/[skill]/SKILL.md` and follow its instructions before writing any code."*).
- Where multiple skills overlap (e.g., accessibility + wcag-audit-patterns, or next-best-practices + nextjs-app-router-patterns), define which skill takes priority or specify that both should be read.
- Review each skill's existing trigger description to ensure the topic keywords in the mapping stay consistent with what the skill actually covers.
- Consider grouping related skills under composite headings (e.g., "Testing" → vitest + playwright-skill) to reduce table size and make the section scannable.

### Expected Outcome

Any agent operating under this AGENTS.md will deterministically invoke the correct skill for a given topic, eliminating reliance on heuristic matching and ensuring consistent, high-quality output aligned with the project's documented patterns.

## Enhancement: Add explicit "execute skill" directives inside each AGENTS-*.md file

### Problem

Each `AGENTS-*.md` file lists related skills under a "Related skills" header, but only as informational references. The agent reads these as context but does not interpret them as an instruction to **go read and follow the skill**. As a result, skill invocation depends entirely on Cursor's automatic heuristic, which can miss or skip skills that directly apply to the work being done.

### Goal

Embed explicit, imperative "execute this skill" directives at the top of each `AGENTS-*.md` file (and in key sections of the main `AGENTS.md`) so that the agent **reads and follows the skill instructions before writing any code**. The format should be an unmissable callout — not a passive reference.

### What should be done

For every file listed below, add an action block (e.g., a blockquote or admonition) near the top of the file or at the start of the relevant section, with language like:

> **Before proceeding, execute the following skill(s)** — read the SKILL.md file and follow its instructions:
> - `.cursor/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`

The specific directives per file:

**`AGENTS.md`** (main file, inside "Common Tasks"):

- **"Add a new entity"** section: execute `drizzle-orm`
- **"Add a UI component"** section: execute `shadcn-ui`, `frontend-design`, `tailwind-v4-shadcn`

**`AGENTS-TESTING.md`**:

- Before writing Vitest unit tests: execute `vitest`
- Before writing Playwright E2E tests: execute `playwright-skill`

**`AGENTS-PATTERNS.md`**:

- Before refactoring component architecture or splitting components: execute `vercel-composition-patterns`
- Before implementing Next.js file-system conventions or App Router patterns: execute `next-best-practices`, `nextjs-app-router-patterns`
- Before optimizing Server Actions or React performance: execute `vercel-react-best-practices`

**`AGENTS-SECURITY.md`**:

- Before implementing or modifying authentication: execute `better-auth-best-practices`
- Before writing or reviewing database queries: execute `drizzle-orm`
- Before hardening Server Actions: execute `vercel-react-best-practices`, `next-best-practices`

**`AGENTS-SEO.md`**:

- Before implementing any SEO feature (metadata, OG images, sitemap, robots): execute `seo`

**`AGENTS-PERFORMANCE.md`**:

- Before implementing caching (`use cache`, PPR, `cacheLife`, `cacheTag`): execute `next-cache-components`
- Before optimizing bundle or rendering performance: execute `vercel-react-best-practices`
- Before adjusting Next.js data patterns or RSC boundaries: execute `next-best-practices`
- Before restructuring component tree for performance: execute `vercel-composition-patterns`

**`AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md`**:

- Before auditing or fixing accessibility: execute `accessibility`, `wcag-audit-patterns`
- Before building or modifying shadcn/ui components with a11y requirements: execute `shadcn-ui`

**`AGENTS-ANIMATIONS.md`**:

- Before designing or implementing animations/visual polish: execute `frontend-design`

**`AGENTS-CONVENTIONS.md`**:

- Before implementing complex type logic, generics, or utility types: execute `typescript-advanced-types`

**`AGENTS-SETUP.md`**:

- Before making schema changes or running Drizzle migrations: execute `drizzle-orm`
- Before configuring Tailwind theme or CSS variables: execute `tailwind-v4-shadcn`

**`AGENTS-PATTERNS-REFERENCE.md`** and **`AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md`**:

- These are reference files read from the main files. Add a note at the top reminding the agent to follow the skill directives from their parent file (`AGENTS-PATTERNS.md` / `AGENTS-TESTING.md`), since the reader was likely sent here from there.

**`AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md`**:

- Same as above — add a note that the skill directives from `AGENTS-SECURITY.md` apply here.

### Format guidance

- The directive should be **imperative and unambiguous**: "Execute the `vitest` skill now" — not "See the `vitest` skill for more info."
- Convert existing "Related skills" sections from passive references into active execution instructions. Don't just add a new block while leaving the old passive reference intact.
- Where multiple skills apply to the same file, order them by relevance (most critical first).
- Keep skill paths explicit (`.cursor/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) so the agent can read them immediately.

### Expected outcome

When the agent reads any `AGENTS-*.md` file during a task, it will encounter an explicit instruction to load the matching skill(s) first, ensuring consistent, high-quality output that follows the project's documented patterns regardless of Cursor's automatic skill detection.
